# Further reading {#sec-further-reading}

- @velleman2019prove
  is a structured introduction to proof techniques
  such as [direct proof](#def-direct-proof), [proof by contradiction](proof-writing.qmd#def-proof-by-contradiction), and induction.
- @barkerplummer2011language
  treats proofs as [formal proofs](#def-formal-proof)
  in [propositional logic](#def-propositional-logic)
  and [first-order logic](#def-first-order-logic).

Free course materials on formal logic:

- Thomas Icard's [Phil 150/250, Mathematical Logic course notes](https://web.stanford.edu/~icard/phil150)
  (Stanford) review sets, relations and functions,
  then cover propositional, modal and first-order logic.
- John Wilcox's [logic handouts](https://www.johnwilcox.org/logic.html)
  supplement the same Stanford course,
  with a handout per week on the syntax and semantics of propositional and first-order logic, natural deduction and metalogic.
- Eric Pacuit's [Phil 151: First Order Logic](https://cs.stanford.edu/~epacuit/classes/phil151winter09.html)
  (Stanford, Winter 2009) posts a syllabus, a modal logic study guide and problem sets.
